rules: Each finding has its own written search of every PubMed record in Europe PMC (titles and abstracts); all reviews, randomised trials and guidelines it found were downloaded.
Left out animal studies (MeSH tags, or the title when there are none) and retracted papers.
A review counts for a finding when the finding's search found it and the finding's words are in its title.

Reviews: meta-analyses or systematic reviews of any design, because most of what is known about habits like walking, sleep or sauna comes from studies that follow people over years, as well as from trials. Chosen: the three newest meta-analyses (systematic reviews only if fewer than three), plus the most comprehensive one (most studies pooled, read from the abstract). Citations are shown but do not choose.
Newer large trials: randomised trials of at least 1,000 people (read from the abstract) from the year of the newest chosen review on, which those reviews may not include.

Historical screening decisions and review choices are retained. Exact screening inputs and per-decision model provenance were not recorded, so they are not validated for current inputs. Legacy file attribution is shown per outcome; these decisions need fresh screening before a new build may select them.
Overlap is not shown: a bibliography can cite background or excluded trials and cannot establish which studies a review included or pooled.

question.outcome: Sudden cardiac death, deaths from heart disease, or death from any cause

screening.by: Claude Code (opus), titles and abstracts only

left.title: Non-acute effects of passive heating interventions on cardiometabolic risk and vascular health: systematic review and meta-analysis of randomized controlled trials
left.reason: Passive heating in adults matches, but outcomes are cardiometabolic and vascular markers, not sudden cardiac, cardiovascular or all-cause death.

left.title: Cardiovascular autonomic modulation during passive heating protocols: a systematic review
left.reason: Passive heating in healthy adults matches, but the outcome is cardiovascular autonomic control (HRV, baroreflex), not death.

left.title: Acute and short-term efficacy of sauna treatment on cardiovascular function: a meta-analysis: reply
left.reason: This is an author reply to a letter, not a systematic review, and there is no abstract reporting mortality outcomes.

left.title: Letter regarding 'Acute and short-term efficacy of sauna treatment on cardiovascular function: a meta-analysis'
left.reason: This is a letter about a meta-analysis, not a systematic review, and there is no abstract reporting mortality outcomes.

left.title: Acute and short-term efficacy of sauna treatment on cardiovascular function: A meta-analysis
left.reason: Sauna exposure matches, but outcomes are acute and short-term cardiovascular function measures, not death, and many participants were patients.
